reason: I checked the sources with lookup.py. 103.1 speaks of 'the loser of the previous game' as one player and has no sentence for several losers (S1, S4). 903.2 and 806 put a Commander game in the Free-for-All variant by default, and nothing there or in 103.1 replaces the choice of who goes first (S2). 800.4 confirms multiplayer games continue as players leave one by one, so losers are ordered in time (S3). The stipulation (S5) fills that gap, and the winner-picks tie-break for simultaneous first losers keeps the chooser a loser and uses no turn order. Its free-for-all limit matches 806.1 and the holding. The draw sentence of 103.1 is untouched (S6): the player who made the choice, first-loser or tie-break pick, chooses again. Holding, each step and the stipulation are as the case words them; I adopt the reasoning as my own.

evidence.excerpt: In a match of several games, the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn. If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.
Unlike two-player games, multiplayer games can continue after one or more players have left the game.
A Commander game may be a two-player game or a multiplayer game. The default multiplayer setup is the Free-for-All variant
In Free-for-All multiplayer games, a group of players compete as individuals against each other.
